assumptions: Single landing burn of the Flight 15 ship catch. SpaceX's published timeline (as reported by Autonocion and Geekspin, Nov 2026) lights three Raptors at T+22:32:16, drops to two at T+22:32:26 while moving between the arms, to one at T+22:32:33 nearly hovering, and the arms close with the last engine cut at T+22:32:34: about 18 s from ignition to catch with no relight. The belly flop speed at ignition follows the Flight 14 broadcast (363 km/h at 1.2 km). Deceleration segments, gains and margins are calibrated against EXOSPHERE to reproduce that sequence; SpaceX did not publish altitudes, speeds or throttle. Ignition point: 380 m short of the tower with no glide plus 13.4 s per m/s of glide toward it, measured on the 215 t bench (850 m at 35 m/s caught). In the game the same lead reached ignition head-on at 22.7 m/s and passed 111 m from the cradle, but the flip throw there (61 m/s) left 75 m/s to brake; a larger lead destabilised the glide loop.
